questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was keen to experience being a part of another culture as well as travel a lot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was easy to find most of the information that was necessary before departure. The hardest information to get was about the courses at my university, because the course catalog wasn't updated at the university, when I had to apply for the merit at KU.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got some assistance from the university in Sydney about the different courses, because I had to change some of them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I moved to Sydney with a friend from KU without having arranged any housing beforehand, as we were told it would be easier to sort out once we were in Sydney. However, it turned out to be quite stressful during the first two weeks to find housing while also starting at the university. In the end, we rented an apartment through an agency, which was very nice. Still, I would highly recommend arranging housing before arriving at your destination.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You need to decide whether you'd prefer to live in the city or closer to the beach. Both options are great, but they offer two very different experiences.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Living in Sydney is expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: If you want to enroll in third-year courses, you need to ensure you meet the prerequisites fo the units. You need to apply for this yourself, and this process can take some time, so make sure to start early.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As an exchange student, you will receive plenty of contact details, which are very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Everything was sorted out as I wanted it to be.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to plan ahead and be on time with the deadlines.

questions.answer: Since I was in Australia, I wanted to travel a lot. Naturally, this was a significant expense during my exchange.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was more expensive than expensive. Sydney is a quite expensive city to live in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any of the social activities, but I know that they had got a lot available including running club, beach volley, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any activities at the host institution, but make sure to set up some surfe lessons, if you like doing stuff like that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go surfing, do plenty of hikes, rent a camper van, and take a road trip along the east coast

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since they speak English, it makes it a lot easier. It was quite easy to adjust to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hmm, I didn't experience any 'particularly' challenging cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They love the nature and outdoor activities. This was really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find a place to live before arriving.
Keep in mind that it gets "quite cold" during winter, so make sure to bring some jackets ;) The houses are not well insulated, so it can feel chilly indoors.
Also, get an international driver’s license in Denmark. It’s necessary if you plan to rent a car in Australia, and it’s much cheaper to obtain in Denmark than in Australia.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring a calculator! You need it for the exams.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To build an everyday life in another country far from home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find a place to live in Sydney.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
